assessment.rationale: A retinal chip that restores useful sight to 43,000,000 patients does not exist, and the field's history is of withdrawal rather than scale-up. The best current result is the PRIMAvera trial of the PRIMA subretinal photovoltaic implant (NEJM 2026): 38 patients implanted for geographic atrophy, 32 assessed at 12 months, clinically meaningful acuity improvement in 26 of them, with 26 serious adverse events in 19 participants, mostly within two months of surgery; explant histology showed minimal tissue response with focal inner retinal atrophy at 18 months, and modelling puts the current 100 micrometre pixel pitch at about 20/420, with 20/80 only if pixels reach 20 micrometres (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=%22subretinal%20implant%22%20AND%20%28PRIMA%20OR%20%22photovoltaic%22%29%20AND%20%22visual%20acuity%22&format=json&pageSize=5&resultType=core). The registry shows the previous generation ending: Argus II post-approval and post-market studies terminated at 52 and 53 patients, Alpha AMS studies withdrawn or terminated, IRIS V2 and NR600 at 10 and 9 patients (https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies?query.intr=retinal+prosthesis+implant&pageSize=15), and the long-term outcome literature now reviews the gap between implant geometry and vision (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=%22Argus%20II%22%20AND%20%28discontinued%20OR%20explant%20OR%20%22long-term%20outcomes%22%29&format=json&pageSize=5&resultType=lite). Open source is one unstarred phosphene simulator (https://api.github.com/search/repositories?q=retinal+prosthesis+simulation&per_page=10&sort=stars). Honest limits: a subretinal photovoltaic array restoring form vision is now published prior art, so rebuilding one is a known answer; the open work is acuity beyond 20/420, surgical risk, device longevity, manufacture and the commercial sustainability that killed Argus II and Alpha AMS.

additionalSearches.finding: PRIMAvera (NEJM 2026): 38 patients implanted with the PRIMA photovoltaic array for geographic atrophy, 32 assessed at 12 months, clinically meaningful acuity improvement in 26 (81 percent), 26 serious adverse events in 19 participants. Histology of four explanted globes showed minimal tissue response with limited focal inner retinal atrophy at 18 months. Modelling gives about 20/420 at the current 100 micrometre pixel pitch, 20/80 only at 20 micrometres.

The previous generation is ending rather than scaling: Argus II post-approval (53) and post-market surveillance (52) studies terminated, two Argus II studies withdrawn, Alpha AMS studies withdrawn or terminated, IRIS V2 (10) and NR600 (9, terminated), with an intracortical visual prosthesis feasibility study recruiting 5. No large or pivotal retinal implant programme is active in this listing.

additionalSearches.query: long-term retinal prosthesis outcomes and resolution limits
additionalSearches.finding: 85 hits including 2026 papers on long-term Argus II outcomes and patient experiences, on determinants of spatial resolution in retinal prostheses and the gap between geometry and vision, on motion perception with visual prostheses, and on brain-computer interface commercialisation. The literature treats durable useful vision and commercial viability as unsettled.
One repository (0 stars), a task-driven phosphene simulator for retinal and cortical prostheses. No open-source implant design, stimulation strategy or clinical system.
